notes.title: The update is available, featuring fixes for steering wheels and controllers!
notes.notes:
We just published another patch for the game. It affects controls, when several controllers are connected at once.

Before, buttons of controllers were read from each controller separately, unlike axles. Because of that, axles’ values could be recognized incorrectly. Now the game can distinguish the axles of the first 4 connected controllers.

But Unity Engine, which the game is built on, can’t guarantee that the controllers will be detected in the exact same order as the previous time. Each new connected controller will be detected as a new one. Probably, we’ll solve this problem a bit later.

You can read more about setting up controllers here:
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2883063682

By the way, Bus World is now 15% off on Steam. If you still haven’t bought the game, it’s now the perfect time!

notes.title: About internal testing and changes to the game
notes.notes:
We decided to start the global internal test of Bus World this week. In the meantime, we tried to play it as it is intended, with game progression, correct order of unlocking scenarios, buses and upgrades. As for now, we are still finding lots of bugs in the game. We have already noticed about 50 problems. Now programmers and level designer will work on fixing them.

Also, we understood that some things may need to be reworked. For example, now gameplay is built on player's level. It means that money is no longer needed - you can't buy anything using it except for gas. So, we decided to make gas free. Player only earns experience points.

Finally, we re-made how the current in-game time is displayed: in old buses, it's shown on the watch which lay near the notebook with schedule. Sometimes, it's hard to read the time without zooming in, so we decided to also show time on the mini-map. It means that you'll be able to see the current time even in 3rd-person mode.

notes.title: Transition to HDRP and release date postponed to 2021
notes.notes:
As we said before, we'd like to make Bus World better than any our games. In order to achieve this, the decision was made to move to the new renderer: HDRP. It was created specifically for ambitious projects with high level of detail. The difference between Built-In (the default Unity renderer which we used before) is noticeable: the picture looks much more "alive" thanks to the new renderer. Take a look at the screenshots which we took in Editor, without anti-aliasing: also, we'd be able to use volumetric lighting.
However, this is a big challenge for our team. It's not that easy to make it as we have to work with new tools and learn how to use them. It's about making night/day cycle, mirrors and plants from scratch. This requires quite a lot of time, and we don't want our game to be released in a buggy state, so we have to postpone the release date to 2021. We'll announce the more accurate release date when we're ready.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36189081/248989c8a5ac60407df604fa81b17d39d991ab1f.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36189081/e90c7913daa3ec459e0ff6244f2a1a667b1dc227.jpg[/img]
